# Who Counts in the Unemployment Rate’s Denominator?

The unemployment rate’s denominator is the labor force: people who are employed plus people classified as unemployed. It does not include everyone who is out of work or considering a job.

The classification depends on a person’s circumstances and job-search activity. Someone on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled can qualify as unemployed without actively searching, provided they meet the availability requirements and the relevant survey reference-period criteria. By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing job listings has not met the active-search criterion.

Being out of work or looking at listings alone does not determine whether someone is counted as unemployed. Those classified as unemployed are included in the labor-force denominator alongside employed people.
